shops.name: Hashigo Honten
shops.name_jp: 支那麺 はしご 本店
shops.description: A spicy ramen restaurant (tantanmen). It's a popular spot so there may be a wait. It stays open late, so the recommendation is to have drinks in Ginza and finish the night off with this ramen.
shops.address: 東京都中央区銀座6-3-5 第二ソワレ・ド・ビル 1F

shops.name: 3chome no Curry yasan
shops.description: A renowned restaurant serving baked cheese beef curry. It gets very crowded during the day, so it is recommended to go right when it opens.
shops.address: 東京都中央区京橋3-9-9 ウィンド京橋ビル B1F

shops.name: Nishimura
shops.description: A long-established tonkatsu restaurant. I once waited in line to get into this place and was approached by an older man behind me, who told me that he had visited tonkatsu restaurants all over the country and this one was the best.
shops.note: May not have English menu and English-speaking staff available.
shops.address: 東京都中央区銀座3-12-6 盛重ビル 1F

shops.name: Tonkatsu Tonki Meguro Honten
shops.name_jp: とんかつ とんき 目黒本店
shops.description: A renowned tonkatsu restaurant with a history of nearly 90 years. There is always a line during the day, but turnover is very fast. Their excellent operation is also a must-see: staff ask for your order when you come in, and what you ordered comes out piping hot as soon as you sit down.
shops.reservation: Dinner only, for groups of 4 or more
shops.address: 東京都目黒区下目黒1-1-2

shops.name: Nico Chelsea
shops.description: A stylish French bistro tucked away in a back alley of Kagurazaka. It specializes in game meat (gibier). Which game is available depends on that day's supply, but every dish is excellent. You can pick your own wine from the wine cellar, which makes it fun. It is a very popular restaurant, so reservations are essential.
shops.address: 東京都新宿区津久戸町3-6

shops.name: Kagurazaka Yakitori Tora
shops.name_jp: 神楽坂 焼鳥 虎
shops.description: A yakitori restaurant on the slightly pricier side for Japan (though still only about $80). The yakitori itself is very good, and the all-you-can-drink plan even includes Yamazaki whisky, so it is great value. It has counter seats only, so going in a small group is recommended. Reservations are essential. Its Tabelog rating is low because it is a new restaurant with few reviews.
shops.address: 東京都新宿区神楽坂2-11 AYビル 1F

shops.name: Dairen (Chinese Home Cooking)
shops.description: A down-to-earth Chinese restaurant that has long been loved by students and office workers. The pan-fried gyoza are very good. It is definitely not the kind of place that appears in travel magazines, so it is recommended if you want to experience a restaurant where local Japanese people go.
shops.address: 東京都港区芝5-15-3 大連ビル

shops.name: Fractale
shops.description: One of the top rum bars in Japan. It is so famous that when it comes to rum in Tokyo, almost every bartender will name this bar. Besides rum, it also has beer and whisky. An authentic bar with a calm atmosphere. Its Tabelog rating is low because it has few reviews; on Tabelog, bars generally tend to get low ratings.
shops.address: 東京都品川区上大崎2-14-3

shops.name: Antonic Nakameguro
shops.description: A small gin bar along the Meguro River. It is a cozy place with only a few counter seats, but you can enjoy gins from all over the world. Gin is also sold in the basement.
shops.address: 東京都目黒区東山1-9-13 東山鈴房荘103

shops.name: Bondy Jimbocho Honten
shops.name_jp: 欧風カレー ボンディ 神保町本店
shops.description: One of the most famous curry restaurants in Japan, and the pinnacle of Japanese-style curry. Rather than strong spices, it is known for the richness and mellowness that come from slowly simmering apples and onions. To everyone from South Asia: this is curry adapted to Japanese tastes, so please forgive us (lol).
shops.address: 東京都千代田区神田神保町2-3 神田古書センター 2F

shops.name: Shanaiya
shops.name_jp: 薬膳スープカレー・シャナイア
shops.description: A restaurant serving yakuzen (medicinal) curry. Despite the name, there is no medicine in it; it is a spice curry made with plenty of ingredients that help with things like recovering from fatigue. Reservations are possible at dinner, but at lunchtime it uses a numbered-ticket waiting system. You can also join the waiting list online, but everyone applies when it opens at 10:30, so you need to be ready at that time.
shops.address: 東京都目黒区三田1-5-5

shops.name: La Maison Dami
shops.name_jp: ラ メゾン ダミ
shops.description: A small French bistro in Meguro. The food is excellent, and the pâté Reo had here was among the best he has ever eaten in his life.
shops.address: 東京都品川区上大崎3-4-9 SEIWAビル 1F

shops.name: Horumon Masaru
shops.description: A Japanese-style BBQ restaurant. Since you grill offal (organ meat), it may not be very familiar to non-Japanese people, but it is very popular among Japanese people. There is not much regular meat, so it is not really recommended for people who do not like offal.
shops.address: 東京都港区芝5-21-14

shops.name: Ramen Taniseya
shops.description: In Japan there is a genre called Yokohama Iekei ramen, based on a pork-bone and soy sauce broth. There are many famous shops in this genre in places such as Yokohama and Shin-Sugita, and this is a well-regarded one that is easy to reach from central Tokyo. There are many Yokohama Iekei shops in Tokyo, but quality varies a lot, so be careful. When you hand over your meal ticket, you can choose the noodle firmness, the strength of the soup and the amount of fat. Reo likes "soft, strong, less fat," but most people generally choose firm noodles.
shops.address: 東京都港区新橋3-11-1 イーグル烏森ビル 1F

shops.name: Menya Kuro
shops.description: A well-regarded Yokohama Iekei shop in Tokyo. For an explanation of Yokohama Iekei, see the description of Ramen Taniseya.
shops.address: 東京都目黒区目黒1-6-12 ワンエム目黒 1F

shops.name: Shinjuku Yakiniku Gyutan no Lemon (Main Shop)
shops.name_jp: 新宿焼肉 牛たんの檸檬 総本店
shops.description: A shop serving thick-cut beef tongue. Many people may be hesitant to eat beef tongue, but its chewy texture is very popular in Japan. We recommend eating it with rice. There are also sister shops besides this one, so please try whichever is easiest to get to.
shops.address: 東京都新宿区西新宿7-16-12 YSビル B1F

shops.name: Bar Tarrow's
shops.description: An authentic bar in Kagurazaka. It has a very large number of whiskies, and the bartender, who has a wealth of experience and knowledge, serves whisky that suits your taste. We don't know how much English he can speak, but he is a wonderful bartender who, we can say for certain, will serve you attentively while using a translation device or similar. Besides whisky, the cocktails are also delicious, and there is a wide variety of rum and other spirits. You can also smoke cigars.
shops.address: 東京都新宿区神楽坂3-6-29 MIビル 3F

shops.name: Shokushuka Okamiya
shops.description: A traditional Japanese izakaya. It is near the house where Reo used to live, and the seafood is very good. A hidden gem loved by locals.
shops.note: We think they can hardly handle English, so you will need to use translation tools or similar.
shops.address: 東京都江東区富岡1-7-10

shops.name: Ramen Benkei (Monzen-Nakacho)
shops.name_jp: らーめん弁慶 門前仲町店
shops.description: There are two flavors: soy sauce and miso. We recommend soy sauce. It is Japanese junk ramen topped with lots of back fat, and the bowls are quite dirty. But the taste is definitely very addictive. Reo ate so much of this ramen that he gained 5 kg. The main shop is in Asakusa, but he has never been there, so he chose this shop.
shops.address: 東京都江東区深川1-1-8

shops.name: Tonkatsu Marushichi
shops.name_jp: とんかつ 丸七 本店
shops.description: In a traditional katsudon, the fried pork is finished by binding it with egg, but the katsudon here is made by preparing the egg and the fried pork separately and placing them on top of the rice. A popular shop that started the so-called "unbound katsudon" boom in Japan. The tonkatsu is very thick, so it has a huge visual impact and looks great in photos. As for the taste, the sauce is quite sweet and the meat is very thick, so it is quite heavy. Recommended for people who love fried food. The line is very long, so you should be in front of the shop when it opens.
shops.address: 東京都江東区門前仲町1-12-5

shops.name: Onigiri Bongo
shops.description: The shop that started an onigiri (rice ball) boom in Japan about five years ago. It was originally a renowned shop known only to those in the know, but its social-media-worthy look went viral and it suddenly became extremely popular. It serves only onigiri and miso soup, and the onigiri packed with fillings and the perfectly cooked rice are very delicious. Honestly, we don't know how popular it is now, but we expect a long line. It seems you can reserve take-out orders, but they seem to accept reservations only by phone, so if you want to make a reservation, please ask Reo.
shops.address: 東京都豊島区北大塚2-27-5 1F

shops.name: Age.3 ASAKUSA
shops.description: A fried sandwich shop. Fried sandwiches themselves became popular after we came to the US, so honestly we are in the same position as all of you. It seems they have not only fruit sandwiches but also ones you could eat for lunch. Judging from the photos, they look delicious, crispy on the outside with a rich seasoning inside. We have quite a lot of free time in Asakusa, so why not stop by?
shops.address: 東京都台東区浅草2-7-22

shops.name: Kitsuneya
shops.description: The gyudon (beef bowl) is simple, but the rich seasoning and the tenderly simmered beef are superb. It opens early in the morning for people who work at the market, but because of that it closes early, at 1 PM, so be careful. Tsukiji is on our schedule, but we may not make it before closing time, so if you want to go here, please let the organizers know.
shops.address: 東京都中央区築地4-9-12

shops.name: I’m donut ? Omotesando
shops.description: Japan's first fresh doughnuts with a fluffy texture. They went viral about a year ago, and our impression is that young people flocked to eat them. The texture is said to be completely different from American doughnuts, so if you are interested, please try them. There are several shops besides Omotesando, so look for a shop that fits your plans.
shops.address: 東京都港区北青山3-5-18

shops.name: Gyukatsu Motomura
shops.name_jp: 牛かつ もと村 渋谷店
shops.description: A shop serving fried beef. In Japan, frying pork or chicken is common, but beef was rare. This shop overturned that convention and succeeded. There are shops not only in Tokyo but also in Osaka and Kyoto, so look for the nearest shop according to your plans.
shops.address: 東京都渋谷区渋谷3-18-10 大野ビル2号館 B1F

shops.name: Kuroge Wagyu Ichinoya Asakusa
shops.name_jp: 黒毛和牛 壱乃屋 浅草
shops.description: Wagyu bowls made with genuine Japanese wagyu. They look very beautiful. It is popular with tourists, but from a Japanese point of view the price is a little too high, so its Tabelog rating is low.
shops.address: 東京都台東区浅草1-34-6 大阪屋ビル 1F

shops.name: Bar CENTIFOLIA
shops.description: A bar extremely focused on looking good on social media. To put it positively, it is the pinnacle of flair bartending, but honestly it goes so far over the top that it makes you laugh. However, the bartender has won a cocktail competition in Japan, and his skill as a bartender is the real thing. If you look at their social media first and are interested, I think it is a place where you can have a special experience.
shops.reservation: Yes, but there is a puzzling reservation fee
shops.address: 東京都港区麻布十番1-6-5 ラミューズ麻布十番ビル 6F

shops.name: Izakaya Aun Akasaka
shops.description: A classic Japanese izakaya with a beautiful interior and a wide range of Japanese dishes. Akasaka is a business district with lots of bars and pubs, so you can drink late into the night. Great place to enjoy solid Japanese Izakaya experience, My previous office was in this area, often hosted client dinners here.
shops.address: 東京都港区赤坂3-21-3 赤坂牧野ビル 1F

shops.name: Nonki BBQ Kagurazaka
shops.name_jp: 神楽坂 たれ焼肉のんき
shops.description: The place I visited most with coworkers. You have to try the garlic-topped beef tongue, "Gari-tongue." It'll get you totally hyped.
shops.address: 東京都新宿区神楽坂3-6-44 神楽坂TKビル 1F

shops.name: Sushi Rin Nishimura Ginza
shops.name_jp: 銀座 凛 にしむら
shops.description: I went onece for wedding anniversary. Exactly what you'd picture a great Japanese sushi restaurant to be. A few counter seats and private rooms, omakase only. The chef is warm and friendly and will chat even with young folks like us. Dinner starts around $200, so it's pricey, but lunch is about $100. If you're in Ginza and want to try serious sushi at least once, start here. Reservation required.
shops.address: 東京都中央区銀座7-2-8 東建ビル B1F

shops.name: Sushi Fukuju Ginza
shops.name_jp: 銀座 鮨 ふくじゅ
shops.description: A typical casual non-conveyor-belt sushi restaurant in Ginza, but with a fairly casual vibe, so you can enjoy high-end sushi without feeling stiff. Lunch omakase starts around ¥10,000, and there's an English menu.
shops.address: 東京都中央区銀座5-8-17 銀座プラザ58ビル 8F

shops.name: Sushi Onodera
shops.description: One of Ginza's best-known sushi restaurants. They're expanding overseas and even have a location in Houston, in a different format. The specialty is Japanese bluefin tuna, and fish delivered daily from Toyosu and Hokkaido is served at a single-plank hinoki counter. Lunch from about ¥8,800, dinner from about ¥27,500. Reservation required.
shops.address: 東京都中央区銀座5-14-14 サンリット銀座ビルⅢ B1F

shops.name: BarTHEHamilton
shops.description: A small authentic bar in Ginza with about 11 seats. They take their cocktails seriously, and you can relax at the counter or on the sofas. Open until 4 AM on weekdays, so it's great for a second or third stop in Ginza. Closed Sundays and holidays.
shops.address: 東京都中央区銀座7-8-14 銀座108ビル 5F

shops.name: Ginza 1954
shops.description: I often came here after work on Fridays with coworkers for the katsu sandwich to recover from the week -their sandwiches are the BEST. Good selection of Japanese and international whisky, and the cocktails and food are excellent too. Open until 3 AM on weekdays, so handy for a late night in Ginza.
shops.address: 東京都中央区銀座8-5-15 SVAX銀座ビル B1F

shops.name: Fish BBQ Ishikawa
shops.description: Fish BBQ. You lightly sear sashimi-grade fish on a tabletop grill and eat it with red-vinegar sushi rice. The signature is the "premium kalbi," which is grilled fatty tuna (otoro). It's a 5-minute walk from Tsukiji Station, so you can pair it with a Tsukiji visit. Reservation required.
shops.address: 東京都中央区築地4-13-5 1F

shops.name: 433 BBQ Roppongi
shops.description: My favorite yakiniku in Roppongi. Fuel up here, then head out into the Roppongi night. Side note: restaurants in Roppongi are generally a bit expensive.
shops.address: 東京都港区六本木4-12-4 飯田ビル 2F

shops.name: Ko-hi en
shops.description: Technically a Chinese restaurant, but it's open until late, so you can come here for a final bowl of noodles after a night out in Roppongi. The soup is mild and mellow, so it's easy on the stomach even late at night.
shops.address: 東京都港区六本木3-8-15 瀬里奈ビレッジ 2F

shops.name: Jumbo BBQ Shirokane
shops.name_jp: 焼肉ジャンボ 白金
shops.description: Near where I used to live. The meat quality is excellent across the board, and it's one of the places I recommend in all of Tokyo!
shops.address: 東京都港区白金3-1-1 第一麻布ビル 1F

shops.name: Yugentei BBQ West Azabu
shops.name_jp: 叙々苑 游玄亭 西麻布本館
shops.description: Probably the most famous high-end yakiniku brand in Japan. The atmosphere is classic Japanese luxury, and the service is top-notch. The food is of course delicious, but honestly it's on par with other great places rather than above them. Best if you want the "I ate at Japan's famous yakiniku spot!" experience.
shops.address: 東京都港区西麻布3-24-18 叙々苑ビル

shops.name: Sushi-ko Azabu
shops.description: The high-end sushi restaurant I visited most with my wife. The chef is quite young relateve to standard, so it doesn't have the formal feel of Ginza sushi restaurants, but he makes each piece with great care. Omakase only, there's a lunch-only 12-piece nigiri course for about ¥16,000. Dinner is ¥32,000 for dinner so quite expensive.
shops.address: 東京都港区麻布十番2-5-3 3F

shops.name: TsuruTonTan UDON NOODLE Brasserie Roppongi
shops.name_jp: つるとんたん UDON NOODLE Brasserie 六本木
shops.description: A famous Japanese udon chain serving very high-quality udon. It's also open late, so you can end the night here with a bowl of udon. When I worked late, I'd often come here for recharge but typically couldn't make it back to office.
shops.address: 東京都港区六本木7-8-6 AXALL ROPPONGI 7F

shops.name: Musashi Ramen Shibuya
shops.name_jp: 麺屋武蔵 武骨外伝
shops.description: This is "tsukemen," a style of ramen where the noodles and soup are served separately and you dip the noodles. The chashu (braised pork) is incredible, so we strongly recommend adding extra chashu. You can also order a huge amount of noodles. The shop has been around since I was in middle school. I would often have 400 g of noodles here on my way home from school or cram school.
shops.address: 東京都渋谷区道玄坂2-8-5

shops.name: Arai-ya BBQ Shibuya
shops.name_jp: 焼肉ホルモン新井屋 渋谷
shops.description: One of my favorite Japanese BBQ spots in Tokyo. Being in Shibuya, it's a bit cramped, so please bear with that. Must-orders are the beef tongue and liver. It has been named to Tabelog's Top 100 Yakiniku list five years in a row. Groups of 8+ must reserve by phone. Reservation required.
shops.address: 東京都渋谷区道玄坂2-19-13

shops.name: Rokkoen BBQ
shops.description: Another of my favorite Japanese BBQ spots in Tokyo. Hmm… everything is just high quality. It's the Tokyo branch of a Kobe restaurant with 50+ years of history, serving Tajima beef from Kobe that's cut after you order. Finish with the "Rokkoen Soup," simmered for 8 hours.
shops.address: 東京都世田谷区池尻2-37-10 石井ビル 1F

shops.name: Bistro Kirakutei
shops.description: A well-known curry spot in Tokyo. The signature is the piping-hot "tsuboyaki" (pot-baked) curry, and the hamburg-steak curry and curry bread are also popular. My parents live nearby, I've been coming here with parents since youth. The taste hasn't changed over the years. It's a 10–15 minute taxi ride from Shibuya, so it's a good lunch option after exploring Shibuya, but there's usually a line, so go early.
shops.address: 東京都世田谷区池尻3-30-5 ニュー池尻マンション

shops.name: BAR Sugahara Shibuya
shops.name_jp: BARすがはら 渋谷本館
shops.description: A bar with a wonderful atmosphere in Shibuya. Instead of a counter, you drink in private rooms, which makes it perfect for a small group that wants a long conversation. They also offer cigars. It's on the edge of Shibuya, so access is a bit inconvenient, but it's open until 4 AM, so it works well as the last stop of a Shibuya night.
shops.address: 東京都渋谷区円山町25-5

shops.name: Open book
shops.description: A bar famous for its lemon sours. The area is called Golden Gai, a maze of tiny bars that's hugely popular with international visitors. Highly recommended for a night out.
shops.address: 東京都新宿区歌舞伎町1-1-6 ゴールデン街五番街

shops.name: Parlor Shiseido
shops.name_jp: 資生堂パーラー 銀座本店 サロン・ド・カフェ
shops.description: Very famous place to have desserts, signature is their fruits parfait. My wife's favorite!
shops.address: 東京都中央区銀座8-8-3 東京銀座資生堂ビル 3F

shops.name: Torichu Iidabashi
shops.description: My personal favorite yakitori spot. Every skewer is delicious, but what I love most is their huge selection of shochu, a Japanese distilled spirit. I'd suggest starting with shochu mixed with soda! Prices are very reasonable, too!
shops.address: 東京都千代田区飯田橋4-7-11 カクタス飯田橋 B1F

shops.name: Kara-Kusa Curry
shops.description: Japanese-style curry. The spices come through, but it is more of a curry where you can taste the natural sweetness of vegetables and other ingredients. The shop has also received a Michelin Guide Bib Gourmand. A small shop with only counter seats. It opened about nine years ago, when Reo was working in Kyoto, and he went there often back then. The service getting more careless every year is a bit of a concern.
shops.address: 京都府京都市下京区綾小路東洞院東入神明町248 グランジュール綾小路 1F

shops.name: Spring Valley Brewery Kyoto
shops.name_jp: スプリングバレーブルワリー京都
shops.description: A brewery with an attached craft beer brewing facility. You can compare different beers in a tasting flight. The menu covers a wide range, from Kyoto-style Japanese food to Western food such as pizza and sausages. A lovely place where you can feel the Kyoto atmosphere along with a modern, stylish vibe.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区富小路通錦小路上る高宮町587-2

shops.name: Tempura Sushi Kaisen Komefuku (Shijo Karasuma)
shops.name_jp: 天ぷら寿司海鮮 米福 四条烏丸店
shops.description: A shop with delicious tempura and seafood. The tempura is not the traditional batter but a crispier, slightly junky style of tempura. Rather than enjoying the tempura on its own with drinks, I personally recommend having it as tendon (tempura rice bowl) for lunch.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区東洞院通錦小路下る阪東屋町658 都証券ビル 1F

shops.name: Kitsune Biyori
shops.description: A shop with delicious tofu and fried tofu (aburaage). Going at night is good too, but they also serve breakfast on weekends, so for those who arrive in Kyoto early, I recommend breakfast. It is also close to the hotel. There is a second shop nearby, but that one does not serve breakfast.
shops.address: 京都府京都市南区東九条西山王町1-6

shops.name: Yokoyama Rosoku
shops.description: A Japanese izakaya in Pontocho that is particular about its sake. The food is also delicious, and you can eat seafood and Japanese dishes that go well with sake. It is a small shop with only counter seats, so it is better to make a reservation.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区西木屋町四条上る紙屋町367-2 たかせ会館 1F

shops.name: Sake to Robata SuSuCoLi
shops.description: A robatayaki shop (fish and vegetables grilled over charcoal). You can fully enjoy the delicious charcoal flavor that only robatayaki can give. Another fun point is that you can drink old-fashioned, nostalgic drinks such as hiyashiame sour and Kyoto akazake bakudan.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区観音堂町474

shops.name: Sui to Sake SUITO (Kyoto Hachijoguchi)
shops.name_jp: 炊と酒 SUITO 京都八条口店
shops.description: They are particular about their rice, and the takikomi gohan (rice cooked with seasonings and ingredients) is delicious. There are also drinks made with fresh fruit, recommended for people who like drinks that taste like juice.
shops.address: 京都府京都市南区東九条北烏丸町3-1 NODE 2F

shops.name: Sakenonki Bingo
shops.description: A Japanese izakaya made by renovating an old Kyoto house. All the food is delicious, but among it all the niku-dofu (beef and tofu simmered together) is superb.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区西錦小路町266

shops.name: Kamadashi Shingobee
shops.description: An Italian restaurant with all-you-can-eat focaccia in five varieties. Its selling point is dishes made in the oven. It is Italian, but it is not a formal restaurant, and you can walk in casually. They also have many drinks other than wine.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区新町通蛸薬師上る六角町370

shops.name: Iroriyaki Bankuba
shops.description: A robatayaki shop (fish and vegetables grilled over charcoal). Another selling point is the live feel of watching the grilling right in front of you.
shops.address: 京都府京都市下京区東塩小路町598-4

shops.name: Yasai to Sakana en
shops.description: A shop focused on vegetables and fish. They are particular about their ingredients, and even simple vegetable dishes are very delicious. They also do robatayaki (fish and vegetables grilled over charcoal).
shops.address: 京都府京都市下京区堺町通綾小路下る永原町153-10

shops.name: Robata to Oden Koronagirai (Kyoto Station)
shops.name_jp: 炉端とおでん 呼炉凪来 京都駅前店
shops.description: An oden shop. Oden is served first as the appetizer, and this oden is all-you-can-eat. Warming up with oden while drinking sake in the cold winter is a classic Japanese winter tradition. Oden is a type of hot pot, and the ingredients are mostly vegetables, fish cakes made from minced seafood, and so on. The ingredients, soaked in a soup full of dashi flavor, are very delicious. There are several shops, so choose one close to your plans.
shops.address: 京都府京都市南区東九条室町48 J'Sビル 5F

shops.name: Oyasai Ryori to Kanmi ISOMATSU (formerly Isomatsu)
shops.name_jp: お野菜料理と甘味 ISOMATSU
shops.description: The exterior looks just like a Japanese restaurant, but it serves dishes that go well with wine. They are especially particular about vegetables. I think it would be classified as Japanese food, but it skillfully fuses Western techniques. I have not tried them, but apparently they also put effort into sweets.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区河原町通四条上る米屋町384

shops.name: Sushi Sho in Kyoto
shops.description: An izakaya where you can eat sushi casually. There are many dishes besides sushi, and you can also eat tempura and more. Recommended for people who want to eat sushi but also want other Japanese food.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区先斗町三条下る材木町184

shops.name: Hyakuen Sushi Stand Enishi
shops.name_jp: 百圓寿司スタンド えにし 烏丸御池店
shops.description: An izakaya where you can drink from noon and eat sushi casually. There are many dishes besides sushi. There are both standing and seated areas, so you can use whichever suits the occasion.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区円福寺町342-1

shops.name: Teppan Futagoya Tominokoji
shops.name_jp: 鉄板 フタゴヤ 富小路
shops.description: A shop where you can eat yakisoba, grilled offal, Japanese omelet and other dishes made on an iron griddle. There are also dishes not made on the griddle, so you can enjoy a Japanese izakaya menu. Note that there is no okonomiyaki.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区富小路通錦小路下る西大文字町615

shops.name: Yuki (Gion)
shops.description: An izakaya run by the Kinkame sake brewery. In addition to many Kinkame sakes, you can enjoy food that goes well with sake. By the way, Kinkame itself is not a famous sake, but it is delicious.
shops.address: 京都府京都市東山区富永町111-1

shops.name: Sushi Sakaba Sashisu
shops.name_jp: 立ちすし酒場 さしす 新梅田食道街店
shops.description: A sushi shop with several locations in Osaka and Kyoto. A popular shop where you can eat delicious sushi casually while standing. There are some booth seats for sitting, but the standing area turns over faster. It is a popular shop that does not take reservations, so unless you go right when it opens, you will have to wait in line for a while.
shops.address: 大阪府大阪市北区角田町9-26 新梅田食道街

shops.name: Menya Inoichi
shops.description: A hugely popular shop selected for the Michelin Bib Gourmand nine years in a row. They are very particular about the soup, and it is so full of dashi flavor that apparently some people end up drinking the whole bowl. The shumai side dish is apparently also delicious, so if you have room, you might want to order it. It is a hugely popular shop and apparently hands out numbered tickets, so I recommend going early. There is apparently also a second shop, so if this shop does not work out, you could try the second shop.
shops.address: 京都府京都市下京区寺町通仏光寺下る恵美須之町542

shops.name: Yasubee
shops.description: A renowned okonomiyaki shop in Pontocho. Besides okonomiyaki, the betayaki, which is a thinly cooked batter topped with cabbage and other ingredients, is apparently also popular.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区先斗町通三条下る梅之木町142

shops.name: WAGYU TERIYAKI ITADAKI BURGER Gion Kyoto
shops.name_jp: WAGYU TERIYAKI ITADAKI BURGER Gion Kyoto
shops.description: A wagyu hamburger shop. It does not have a website for Japanese customers and is aimed entirely at overseas tourists. Perhaps because of that, the prices are on the high side for Japan, which I personally don't like, but its Google Maps rating is an astonishing 5.0. Having a 5.0 with more than 3,000 reviews is honestly impressive. The taste is probably the real deal.
shops.address: 京都府京都市東山区廿一軒町 祇園華月ビル 1F

shops.name: Mensho Takamatsu
shops.name_jp: 麺匠 たか松 本店
shops.description: The main shop of a ramen chain with locations across Japan. The ramen is delicious too, but I would like to recommend the tsukemen (dipping noodles). The dipping sauce, a chicken base with seafood dashi and more added, is very delicious. They use stone-ground whole wheat noodles, which have a stronger wheat flavor than normal noodles and go down smoothly. Onions and sudachi (a Japanese citrus) are served on a separate plate, so after eating some, you can add these toppings to change the flavor and enjoy it from start to finish. There are several shops, so go to one close to you.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区一蓮社町312

shops.name: Kichi Kichi
shops.description: A shop famous for omurice (fried rice topped with soft, half-cooked egg). Of course it tastes good, but it is also a dish you can enjoy even before eating because it looks so beautiful. First, please look at the actual omurice on their website or elsewhere. It is reservation only, and you cannot get in without a reservation, so be careful. However, I don't like that they charge $13 just to make a reservation.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区三条先斗町下る材木町185-4

shops.name: Rokujuan
shops.description: A shop where you can enjoy traditional Japanese tea sweets and tea (matcha, hojicha and more). The hana warabi is truly beautiful, and the shop shows well the character of Japanese sweets, which are also particular about appearance. It seems you can also have meals, but here please be sure to enjoy the Japanese sweets.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区六角通新町西入西六角町101

shops.name: Mi mitarashi-dango
shops.description: A dango shop. They also have traditional-style dango, but what makes this shop popular is its photogenic, beautiful-looking dango. They put sweet bean paste shaped like seasonal flowers on top of the dango. They also have traditional-style dango, but rather than those, please order the beautiful-looking hanamari dango.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区槌屋町89

shops.name: Gion Tsujiri (Gion Main Shop)
shops.name_jp: 祇園辻利 祇園本店
shops.description: A matcha shop. One of the most famous matcha shops in Japan. They serve not only matcha for drinking in the original style but also matcha lattes and matcha-flavored sweets. They post a lot of photos on Instagram, but honestly I don't think they are very good. The real thing must be much nicer.
shops.address: 京都府京都市東山区祇園町南側573-3

shops.name: Nakamura Tokichi Main Shop
shops.description: A matcha shop. Probably the most popular shop in the Uji area, with the longest lines. They have matcha, but they are famous for parfait-like sweets with matcha ice cream, jelly, shiratama (rice flour dumplings) and more in a traditional Japanese vessel. Even if you go right when it opens, you may wait in line for more than an hour, so please go prepared. There are also shops around Kyoto Station and Gion.
shops.address: 京都府宇治市宇治壱番10

shops.name: Itohkyuemon Uji Main Shop and Tea Room
shops.name_jp: 伊藤久右衛門 宇治本店・茶房
shops.description: Along with Nakamura Tokichi Main Shop, a popular matcha shop in the Uji area. The matcha sweets are famous, but you can also eat soba with tea kneaded into the noodles. It is a popular shop, so it is crowded, and please be prepared for a considerable wait. There is also a shop in Gion, so you don't have to go all the way to Uji.
shops.address: 京都府宇治市莵道荒槇19-3

shops.name: Saryo Tsujiri (Gion Main Shop)
shops.name_jp: 茶寮都路里 祇園本店
shops.description: A popular matcha shop. There are shops around Kyoto Station and Gion.
shops.address: 京都府京都市東山区祇園町南側573-3 祇園辻利本店 2F・3F

shops.name: Kyoto Tonkatsu Katsuda (Shijo Kawaramachi)
shops.name_jp: 京都とんかつ かつ田
shops.description: A popular tonkatsu (fried pork) shop. Besides tonkatsu, its fried beef is apparently also famous.
shops.address: 京都府京都市下京区稲荷町330-2 京都和牛館 1F

shops.name: Shinpuku Saikan Main Shop
shops.description: A long-established, popular shop famous for its pitch-black soup. The soup, based on chicken bones and pork bones with a strong soy sauce flavor, is addictive. The thin noodles are smooth, go down easily, and are easy to finish. The fried rice, also soy sauce based, is delicious too, so if you have room, I recommend ordering both. There is also a branch in Osaka.
shops.address: 京都府京都市下京区東塩小路向畑町569

shops.name: Ajinoya Main Shop
shops.description: A renowned okonomiyaki shop. They use more cabbage and a little less batter, but the whole thing is fluffy and light to eat. A popular shop that is also listed in the Michelin Bib Gourmand. Honestly, okonomiyaki is delicious anywhere, but I thought this one was especially delicious.
shops.address: 大阪府大阪市中央区難波1-7-16 2F

shops.name: Unagiya Hirokawa
shops.description: A renowned eel shop in Arashiyama. The unaju, eel grilled over charcoal with a sweet and salty sauce and placed on rice, is exceptionally delicious. As a snack with drinks, there is also unagi shirayaki (eel grilled without sauce), which comes without sauce or rice. Reo likes to share the shirayaki with the people he goes with, have everyone order their own unaju, and share bottled beer among everyone. There is also a shop in the Kawaramachi area. Reservations only, so be careful.
shops.address: 京都府京都市右京区嵯峨天龍寺北造路町44-1

shops.name: Kikunoi Main Restaurant
shops.name_jp: 京料理 菊乃井 本店
shops.description: A kaiseki restaurant that has earned three Michelin stars. You can enjoy a Japanese course meal in which each dish is carefully prepared. A place to enjoy a calm meal in a luxurious, Kyoto-style Japanese room. It is a high-end restaurant, so Reo has never been, but it is the kind of place you would want to go to someday. Reservations only.
shops.address: 京都府京都市東山区下河原通八坂鳥居前下る下河原町459

shops.name: Fukutaro Main Shop
shops.description: A renowned okonomiyaki shop in the Namba area. Listed in the Michelin Bib Gourmand. Besides okonomiyaki, the negiyaki (green onion pancake) is apparently also delicious. There are also shops in Umeda and other places.
shops.address: 大阪府大阪市中央区千日前2-3-17

shops.name: Yakko
shops.description: A kushikatsu shop in the Shinsekai area. Kushikatsu is a dish of vegetables, seafood or meat on skewers, coated in batter and deep-fried. The ingredients here are apparently large and delicious. Dipping a skewer back into the sauce after taking a bite is prohibited, so don't do it.
shops.address: 大阪府大阪市浪速区恵美須東2-3-10

shops.name: Takoyaki Doraku Wanaka (Sennichimae Main Shop)
shops.name_jp: たこ焼道楽 わなか 千日前本店
shops.description: A popular takoyaki shop. They have a fluffy texture and are gooey inside, and delicious. Listed in the Michelin Bib Gourmand. There are shops in various places.
shops.address: 大阪府大阪市中央区難波千日前11-19

shops.name: Tabutchan
shops.name_jp: 屋台担担麺 たぶっちゃん
shops.description: A spicy tantanmen shop in the Nipponbashi area. It is open until late at night, so I recommend it as a bowl to finish the night. It is extremely spicy, so people who can't handle spicy food should avoid it.
shops.address: 大阪府大阪市中央区千日前1-6-1 1F

shops.name: Pontocho Kiraku BBQ
shops.name_jp: 先斗町焼肉 きらく
shops.description: A yakiniku restaurant in Pontocho famous for its "negi-tan shio," salted beef tongue piled with green onions. It's a popular chain with branches in Roppongi and Osaka. Don't miss the beef hitsumabushi (rice bowl) at the end.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区先斗町通三条下る2丁目若松町139-2

shops.name: Pontocho Kiraku Shabushabu
shops.name_jp: 先斗町しゃぶしゃぶすき焼き きらく
shops.description: The sister restaurant of Kiraku above, serving shabu-shabu and sukiyaki. You can enjoy premium beef such as Kobe beef, and the Inaniwa udon to finish is also highly rated. You can't go wrong with either Kiraku.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区先斗町通四条上る柏屋町169-2

shops.name: Iroha Sukiyaki
shops.name_jp: すきやき いろは 北店
shops.description: A sukiyaki restaurant in Pontocho. You can enjoy Kyoto beef sukiyaki in a private tatami room overlooking the city. Great if you want sukiyaki in a classic Kyoto setting. Some say the portions are a bit small, so consider ordering extra meat.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区先斗町四条上ル鍋屋町215

shops.name: Okaru Udon Gion
shops.description: A long-standing udon shop. Honestly the taste isn't anything special, but the atmosphere is calming. In the cold months, I often ate here on my way home from school great place.
shops.address: 京都府京都市東山区八坂新地富永町132

shops.name: Yamamoto Menzo  Udon
shops.description: Personally, I think it's the best udon in Kyoto. It's a bit outside the center, but highly recommended. The line is very long, so be prepared. I believe there's another soba or udon shop right next door, and that one's good too.
shops.address: 京都府京都市左京区岡崎南御所町34

shops.name: Emon Sushi
shops.description: Where I worked part-time during undergrad! It's far from the main nightlife area, and I wouldn't say the food is anything special, but you can enjoy a full range of sushi and seafood at reasonable prices. I haven't been back since undergrad lol.
shops.address: 京都府京都市上京区田中町415

shops.name: Kani Doraku
shops.name_jp: かに道楽 京都本店
shops.description: Kani Doraku is a crab restaurant chain found all over Japan. The food never disappoints and the interior is very luxurious; I love this place. It's right in the middle of Kyoto's downtown, so there will be plenty of tourists, but I don't think it has fully sold out to tourism.
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区三条通寺町西入天性寺前町525

shops.name: Torisei Kiyomizu
shops.description: The Kiyomizu branch of Torisei, a well-known chicken restaurant run by a Fushimi sake brewery. Yakitori and oyakodon (chicken and egg rice bowl) are popular, and prices are reasonable. It's easy to stop by after visiting Kiyomizu-dera or Yasaka Shrine. No reservations, so heads up.
shops.address: 京都府京都市東山区東大路松原上る辰巳町114

shops.name: Gyoza Hohei
shops.name_jp: ぎょうざ歩兵 祇園本店
shops.description: Gyoza in Kyoto? You might think so, but this is a great spot for delicious gyoza at a reasonable price.
shops.address: 京都府京都市東山区清本町373-3

shops.name: Shimogamo Saryo
shops.description: A long-established Kyoto cuisine (kaiseki) restaurant near Shimogamo Shrine. You can enjoy a course of Kyoto vegetables and seasonal ingredients while looking out over a Japanese garden. It's pricey, but recommended if you want to experience authentic Kyoto-style Japanese cuisine at least once.
shops.address: 京都府京都市左京区下鴨宮河町62

shops.name: Demachi Futaba
shops.description: Not a restaurant but a Japanese sweets (wagashi) shop. A friend of mine worked here part-time. It was popular back then, but now it's insanely popular. You'll definitely have to wait in line, but the true taste of Kyoto wagashi is right here!
shops.address: 京都府京都市上京区出町通今出川上ル青龍町236

shops.name: Tonryu North Shirakawa
shops.description: It's on the outskirts of Kyoto, so it'll be hard to visit during the Trek, but it's the place I went to most in undergrad, so let me at least introduce it! A gentle flavor you won't find anywhere else.
shops.address: 京都府京都市左京区北白川上別当町1 第2青山荘 1F

shops.name: Tenka Ippin Main store
shops.description: Japan has a ramen chain called Tenkaippin, and its flagship store is here on the outskirts of Kyoto. It'll be hard to visit during the Trek, but it's a pilgrimage site for Japanese ramen fans, so I'm including it. Go if you get the chance!
shops.address: 京都府京都市左京区一乗寺築田町94 メゾン白川 1F

shops.name: Toriyasu
shops.description: Kyoto is known for its delicious dashi (Japanese soup stock made from kombu and bonito flakes), which is why I personally think Kyoto oyakodon is so good. Both the oyakodon and the karaage (fried chicken) here are excellent. It's not a touristy place, so recommended from that perspective. Heads up: they're only open for lunch, so plan to go at midday!
shops.address: 京都府京都市中京区烏丸通押小路角（秋野々町534）

shops.name: Manjiro Nabe
shops.description: A mizutaki (chicken hot pot) specialty restaurant in Gion. Many say the milky chicken broth hot pot is amazing all the way through to the rice porridge (zosui) at the end. Dinner is reservation-only and a bit pricey, but lunch serves oyakodon for under ¥2,000, so it's a good lunch option too.
shops.address: 京都府京都市東山区新橋通大和大路東入元吉町58

shops.name: Toshinoya
shops.name_jp: 府中焼き としのや 堺町店
shops.description: A somewhat unusual type of Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki, with the noodles grilled until crispy. Because the noodles are crispy, you can eat it almost like a snack, and it is excellent as a bar snack with drinks. When Reo goes to Hiroshima, he ends up going only here. There are about 10 shops in Hiroshima, and considering the schedule that day, the Hiroshima Station-front shop or the Sakaimachi shop is recommended.
shops.address: 広島県広島市中区堺町1-3-14 SAKURA14ビル 1F

shops.name: Chuka Soba Yoki
shops.name_jp: 中華そば 陽気 大手町店
shops.description: Old-fashioned soy sauce ramen. It looks simple, but the soup, made with pork bone stock, is rich and full-bodied. The chashu topping is juicy and delicious, and the crunch of the bean sprouts whets the appetite. There are several shops, but given the schedule that day, the Hiroshima Station-front shop or the Otemachi shop is recommended. I have never been to the Hiroshima Station-front shop, but for some reason its Google Maps rating is low, which concerns me.
shops.address: 広島県広島市中区大手町3-1-6

shops.name: Okonomiyaki Nagataya
shops.description: The classic style of Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki. You enjoy the chewy noodles and cabbage together, and the generous amount of green onions adds an accent and is delicious. Another good point is that it is close to the meeting place after free time.
shops.address: 広島県広島市中区大手町1-7-19 重石ビル 1F

shops.name: Ramen Muroka
shops.description: A wonton chuka soba shop that uses wontons (something like boiled dumplings) instead of noodles. It is not ordinary ramen, so be aware, but it is a shop with delicious soup full of seafood dashi flavor. By the way, ramen with regular noodles is also available in limited quantities.
shops.address: 広島県広島市中区三川町10-18

shops.name: Men Yohaku
shops.description: One of Hiroshima's best ramen shops, which has also been listed in the Michelin Bib Gourmand. Elegant soy-sauce-based ramen.
shops.address: 広島県広島市中区西十日市町2-15

shops.name: Yakigaki no Hayashi
shops.description: A shop on Miyajima where you can eat oysters. You can have grilled oysters, raw oysters and steamed oysters. Hiroshima is one of Japan's leading oyster-producing areas. Apparently you cannot place an additional order once you have ordered, so be careful.
shops.address: 広島県廿日市市宮島町505-1

shops.name: Miyajima Anagomeshi Mametanuki
shops.name_jp: 宮島あなごめし まめたぬき
shops.description: A shop where you can eat anago meshi, a Hiroshima specialty. A superb dish of conger eel dipped in a sweet and salty soy-sauce-based sauce, grilled, and placed on rice.
shops.address: 広島県廿日市市宮島町1133 錦水館 1F

shops.name: Okonomiyaki Hassho
shops.description: Classic-style Hiroshima okonomiyaki. It seems to be a popular shop with fairly long lines, but apparently turnover is good. Apparently they only accept cash, so be careful!
shops.address: 広島県広島市中区幟町14-17

shops.name: Ekohiiki
shops.description: A shop where you can eat dishes made with Hiroshima ingredients. Famous dishes include anago meshi, conger eel dipped in a sweet and salty soy-sauce-based sauce, grilled and placed on rice, and oysters, but you can also eat many other local specialties. Another good point is that it is close to the next meeting place.
shops.address: 広島県広島市中区大手町1-7-20 小松ビル 1F
